markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's consolidated control over the Chinese Communist Party, military, and state institutions, reinforced by the 2018 removal of presidential term limits, underpins trader consensus that he will remain in power through 2026. No scheduled leadership transition exists before the 21st Party Congress expected in late 2027, and recent developments—including his active diplomatic engagements, policy directives into 2026, and appointments of loyal officials—show no signs of elite challenge or forced exit. Speculation around health or succession has not altered this positioning, as analysts note the absence of viable mechanisms or rivals capable of prompting an earlier change. Rare developments such as a severe health crisis, major economic collapse triggering elite revolt, or an internal power struggle could still shift probabilities before the congress.
